title: Post Double-Team Rotation
description: A team practises sending a quick double-team at a strong post player near the rim, then rotating to cover the open perimeter player the double leaves behind.

content.objective: Double-team near the rim safely and rotate the rest of the defense to cover the gap.
content.setup: A post player receives the ball on the block against a single defender, with a second defender ready to help.
instructions: The post defender holds position as the help defender pushes in for a quick double.
The double-team must be brief and active, not a long-held trap.
The remaining defenders rotate one spot to cover the help defender's original matchup.
If the post kicks out, the defense recovers to close out on the new ball handler.
coachingPoints: Keep the double-team short — a long one gives up an easy pass.
Rotate immediately once the double is sent, not after the pass.
Communicate who is rotating to cover which open player.
commonMistakes: Leaving the double on too long and conceding an easy kick-out shot.
No one rotating to cover the gap the double-team created.
Talking too little for teammates to react in time.
content.safety: Double-team with active hands only, no grabbing or pushing the post player's chair.
